requirements.title: Successful pointer allocation creates a target and associates the pointer with it
requirements.definition: Allocation of a pointer creates an object that implicitly has the TARGET attribute. After successful ALLOCATE for a pointer, the pointer is associated with the target and can be used to reference or define it. Additional pointers can become associated with that pointer target or a part of it by pointer assignment, and ASSOCIATED can be used to determine whether a pointer with defined association status is associated.

pending.pointer-associated-after-allocate: PENDING complete source allocating an INTEGER pointer with STAT=0, then observing ASSOCIATED(p)=.TRUE. and assigning literal 91 through p. The pointer status is defined before ASSOCIATED is called.
pending.allocated-target-reference-and-definitio: PENDING complete source allocating a pointer, defining p=92, then referencing p in a literal comparison. The oracle is value 92 and reached sentinel; p is associated before definition and reference.
pending.allocated-target-implicit-target-for-oth: PENDING complete source allocating pointer p, assigning p=93, then pointer-assigning q=>p or q=>a part of p under 10.2.2 and observing q associated and q value 93. This demonstrates the allocated object is a valid target without address arithmetic.
pending.associated-inquiry-after-defined-status: PENDING complete source comparing ASSOCIATED on a pointer immediately after ALLOCATE and after NULLIFY in a separate control, observing true then false only when association status is defined. No ASSOCIATED call is made for an undefined pointer.
pending.bounds-type-parameters-of-pointer-target: PENDING complete source allocating a pointer array or deferred-length character pointer with explicit bounds or length, observing LBOUND/UBOUND/LEN inquiry results and a defined literal value. The allocation form itself remains 9.7.1.1/9.7.1.2 owned.

requirements.title: Allocating an already associated pointer creates a new target and breaks the previous association
requirements.definition: It is not an error to allocate a pointer that is already associated with a target. A new pointer target is created as required by the pointer attributes and ALLOCATE-specified array bounds, type, and type parameters; the pointer becomes associated with the new target; any previous association is broken; and a previous target created by allocation becomes inaccessible unless other pointers remain associated with it.

pending.reallocate-associated-pointer-not-error: PENDING complete source allocating pointer p, assigning literal 101, then allocating p again with STAT=0 without prior NULLIFY or DEALLOCATE. The oracle is STAT=0 for the second allocation and successful assignment of a distinct literal 102 through p.
pending.new-target-has-new-allocation-characteri: PENDING complete source first allocating pointer array p(1:2), then allocating p(5:7), observing after the second allocation LBOUND=5, UBOUND=7, SIZE=3 and new literal values. The changed bounds make the new target material.
pending.previous-association-broken: PENDING complete source preserving another pointer q=>p before reallocating p. After reallocating p and assigning p=111 while q still has old value 110, the oracle is distinct p and q literals through standard pointer association, not addresses. If no q is kept, the old allocated target is not probed.
pending.previous-target-retained-only-through-ot: PENDING paired source: one case keeps q associated with the old target and observes q literal after p is reallocated; a source-only classification notes that without such a pointer the old target is inaccessible and cannot be used as an executable oracle. No storage leak or address check is proposed.

requirements.title: Pointer function results must return with associated or disassociated status
requirements.definition: At the beginning of execution of a function whose result is a pointer, the association status of the result pointer is undefined. Before such a function returns, it shall either associate a target with this pointer or cause this pointer association status to become disassociated.

pending.result-associated-before-return: PENDING complete source defining a pointer-valued function that associates its result with a saved TARGET literal 121 before return, then observing ASSOCIATED(f()) through assignment to a pointer or direct permitted use and the literal value. The target lifetime and pointer-result interface are dependencies.
pending.result-disassociated-before-return: PENDING complete source defining a pointer-valued function that executes NULLIFY on its result before return, then pointer-assigning the result to a pointer and observing ASSOCIATED=.FALSE. The oracle is disassociated status with defined association, not undefined status.
pending.return-without-defined-association-inval: PENDING diagnostic/control source for a pointer-valued function that returns without associating or nullifying the result, repaired by adding only NULLIFY(result). The repaired oracle is ASSOCIATED=.FALSE.; the invalidity is attributed to S9.7.1.4-003 and the invalid result is not queried or dereferenced.
